ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown, \(O\) is the intersection point of the diagonals of rhombus \(ABCD\), \(DE \parallel AC\), \(CE \parallel BD\). If \(AC = 6\), \(BD = 8\), then what is the length of line segment \(OE\)?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given $\because$DE$\parallel$AC, CE$\parallel$BD,\\
$\therefore$ quadrilateral OCED is a parallelogram,\\
$\because$ quadrilateral ABCD is a rhombus,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$COD$=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ quadrilateral OCED is a rectangle,\\
Further $\because$AC$=6$, BD$=8$,\\
$\therefore$OC$=3$, OD$=4$,\\
$\therefore$CD$=\sqrt{OC^{2}+OD^{2}}=\sqrt{3^{2}+4^{2}}=\boxed{5}$,\\
In rectangle OCED, OE$=CD=5$.

Further, because \(AC = 6\) and \(BD = 8\), therefore \(OC = 3\) and \(OD = 4\). Thus, \(CD = \sqrt{OC^{2}+OD^{2}} = \sqrt{3^{2}+4^{2}} = \boxed{5}\). In rectangle \(OCED\), \(OE = CD = 5\).
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, quadrilateral ABCD is a rhombus, A is above, C is below, B is on the left side, and D is on the right side. Diagonal AC is vertical, BD is horizontal, and they intersect at point O. Point E is located at the lower right, CE is a horizontal line segment, and DE is a vertical line segment, so E is the lower-right corner point formed by the line through C parallel to BD and the line through D parallel to AC. Reasoning: Using the coordinate method, take O as the origin, let BD be the horizontal axis, and AC be the vertical axis. Because ABCD is a rhombus, the diagonals bisect each other, and AC = 6, BD = 8, so OC = 3, OD = 4. From the positions in the figure, C is below O and D is to the right of O, therefore we can take C = (0, -3), D = (4, 0). Also DE ∥ AC, so DE is vertical; CE ∥ BD, so CE is horizontal, therefore E = (4, -3). Thus OE = sqrt((4 - 0)^2 + (-3 - 0)^2) = sqrt(16 + 9) = 5.
